comments.body:
Thanks. Emitting `--trusted-host` here is the right fix, but two changes, please:

1. **Share the logic with install.** `_print_trusted_host` repeats `_add_trusted_host_if_needed` from `prepare_pip_source_args` in `pipenv/utils/indexes.py`. Please factor out one module-level helper (for example `trusted_host_for_source(url, verify_ssl) -> str | None`) and use it in both places. Otherwise `pipenv install` and `pipenv requirements` can drift apart again, which is how this bug happened in the first place.

2. **Env-var hosts get lowercased.** `parse_url` lowercases the host:

   ```python
   >>> parse_url("https://${PRIVATE_HOST}/simple").host
   '${private_host}'
   ```

   So a source with `url = "https://${PRIVATE_HOST}/simple"` produces `--trusted-host ${private_host}`, which won't expand (env-var names are case-sensitive on POSIX), while the `-i` line next to it keeps `${PRIVATE_HOST}`. Either take the host from the original string or skip `--trusted-host` when the host is an env var, and add a test case for it.

Thanks for the review. Both done in 48e1e39: `trusted_host_for_source(url, verify_ssl)` in `pipenv/utils/indexes.py` is now used by `prepare_pip_source_args` and by `pipenv requirements`; when the host is an env var it is taken from the original string (`--trusted-host ${PRIVATE_HOST}`), with a requirements test for `https://${PRIVATE_HOST}/simple` (lock and `--no-lock`) and unit cases for the helper. The description is updated.

This comment was drafted with the help of an AI agent (Claude) working on behalf of the PR author.
